title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-node-pools-iam-networking-migration
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments currently maintain per-customer Terraform state and slightly divergent module layouts for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking. This has made upgrades, cross-customer automation, and state migrations error-prone during installer and on-prem upgrades. This PR unifies the Terraform state layout and module interfaces used by the private installer and the terraform modules repo, adds explicit migration tooling, and documents rollout/rollback steps. Changes: 1) Introduce a unified state layout module (modules/state-layout) with an opt-in migration path that maps legacy per-environment state keys to the new canonical layout. 2) Rename and normalize GPU node pool module inputs/outputs (modules/gpu-node-pools) to use consistent naming across GCP/AWS/AZURE providers, add node group tagging for runtime autoscaler, and add safe replacement plan behavior. 3) Centralize IAM role definitions (modules/iam) and split role bindings vs. role templates to ease audit/attachment in private deployments. 4) Network module refactor (modules/networking) to preserve existing VPC/subnet IDs where provided and to support both shared-vpc and dedicated-vpc layouts. 5) Add a migration helper script (scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh) that performs a dry-run, produces a mapping manifest, and can be used with the installer to orchestrate a zero-downtime state rename. 6) Update examples/ and docs/ with an explicit upgrade checklist and rollback steps. Migration plan and rollout: The migration is opt-in per-customer. The installer will default to legacy layout unless the new flag is provided. Documented migration steps include: run dry-run mapping, snapshot current remote state, apply mapping with lock/leader election, validate resources unchanged (plans only), then flip the installer flag and run apply. Rollback: revert to snapshot and re-run installer against legacy layout. Testing: added unit tests for module input validation, terraform validate/plan CI gates, and an integration test that performs a tfstate mapping dry-run against a small synthetic state. Backwards compatibility: inputs are provided with compatibility shims; default behavior is unchanged until operator opts in. Risk and mitigation: state renames are high-risk; we added mandatory state snapshots, explicit locking, and a staged rollout with runbook. See RELEASE NOTES and docs for full operational instructions. Checklist: - [x] design reviewed by Infra and SRE - [x] linear tickets linked - [x] migration script tested locally - [x] CI plan/validate passes - [x] docs updated

release_notes: Unify private Terraform state layout for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking.
Add opt-in migration tooling and documented upgrade/rollback runbook.
Normalize GPU node pool module interfaces across cloud providers.
Split IAM role templates and bindings for clearer auditability.
